question: Why did site traffic drop 17% on 2024-03-02 compared with the day before?

steps.name: plan
steps.title: Plan: sessions on 2024-03-02
steps.detail: Pull daily sessions for 2024-03-02 and 2024-03-01 to confirm the 17% drop and its size. | Break the sessions change down by region, platform and channel to find where the loss is concentrated. | Check whether the drop matches a normal repeating pattern such as a weekday or weekend effect. | Search the deploy changelog, GitHub issues and support tickets for releases, outages or campaign changes around 2024-03-01 to 2024-03-02. | Summarize the most likely cause type (bad_deploy, regional_outage, platform_bug, campaign_end or seasonality) with the supporting evidence and metric IDs.

steps: Pull daily sessions for 2024-03-02 and 2024-03-01 to confirm the 17% drop and its size.
Break the sessions change down by region, platform and channel to find where the loss is concentrated.
Check whether the drop matches a normal repeating pattern such as a weekday or weekend effect.
Search the deploy changelog, GitHub issues and support tickets for releases, outages or campaign changes around 2024-03-01 to 2024-03-02.
Summarize the most likely cause type (bad_deploy, regional_outage, platform_bug, campaign_end or seasonality) with the supporting evidence and metric IDs.

steps.name: detect_anomaly
steps.title: detect_anomaly: sessions on 2024-03-02
steps.detail: sessions on 2024-03-02 (Saturday) was 1.645e+05. The same weekday in the 6 weeks before had a median of 1.625e+05. Change vs that baseline: +1.2% (z = +1.2). Change vs the day before: -16.7%. This is within the normal range for this weekday, so it is not an anomaly.

steps.name: investigate
steps.title: Finished investigating
steps.detail: The 17% drop on 2024-03-02 is a normal weekend dip (seasonality), not an incident. Saturday's sessions were 164.5k, within 1.2% of the median for prior Saturdays (z = +1.2), and no region, platform or channel stands out (M1, M2). No deploy, outage or campaign search is needed.

steps.detail: Normal weekend dip in sessions on Saturday

output.summary: Sessions fell about 17% on 2024-03-02 compared with the day before, but that day was a Saturday. Sessions were within the normal range for a Saturday, so the drop reflects the usual weekday pattern rather than an incident.
